design_purpose_combat_skills: D-016: skills are learned, not worn. Each entry is one skill: its delivery (the engine's shape: cone, strike, projectile, dash), its tags (what modifiers and hooks latch onto) and its payload numbers. `starting` skills are the base kit (a character with no class yet: tests and harnesses); a class chosen before play (foundry.json rails.classes[].starting_skills, 4 Sep 2026) replaces them with its own kit and fills the bar in that order - a bow shot for the Ranger, strikes for the Warden, a bolt and a sweep for the Kindler - and the base skills a class does not carry become pages. The rest are learned from skill pages that mobs drop, weighted by drop_weight among the skills the player does not know yet. Gear never grants a skill - it only scales skills by tag. MELEE (4 Sep 2026, Wave 5 item 11): a strike or a sweep carries stagger_seconds (the mob it hits halts that long and loses its wind-up), push_m (it is shoved that far back, along the blow) and swing_armour for swing_seconds (the armour committing to the swing grants you, on the same clock as the Plate reading's armour on cast); bosses take grammar.json hooks.melee's fractions of the stagger and the push. All three resolve through the grammar (add_stagger, add_push, add_armour_on_cast), so gear and the plate can grow them.

combat_skills.description: A quick, straight arrow with light bleed. Pick off a pursuer while keeping your distance.
combat_skills.design_purpose: The Ranger's opener (owner, 4 Sep 2026: 'more initial skills, not frost orb - a bow shot'): a quick physical projectile that is an ATTACK, so Frostbite and the shatter rules read it, with a little bleed so the Quarry rail and the Edge ingot have something to sharpen. Thin and fast like the bolt; the skill is the line, not the lead.

combat_skills.description: Sweep fire across the nearby front. Catch a gathered pack and build ignite.
combat_skills.design_purpose: The Kindler's close answer: a burning sweep in front (the player's cone) that is an ATTACK of fire, so it shatters a frozen ring and lights the packs the bolt cannot single out. Its ignite builds slower than the bolt's; Kindling and the Pyre rail are where it pays.

combat_skills.description: Strike a close group in front and push it back. Make room when the train closes in.

mastery.text: the sweep reaches a little further

combat_skills.description: A committed close blow that staggers and shoves one enemy. Swing armour helps you hold your ground.
A slow orb builds chill and forks toward fresh targets. Freeze a gathered train before an attack cashes it in.
combat_skills.design_purpose: The grammar sentence opener: an orb that forks on impact and stacks chill toward the freeze threshold. Its damage is modest on purpose - the payoff lives in the freeze-shatter combo, not the hit. Cooldown 1.2 against chill decay 6/s means a bare caster freezes on the third orb; Deep Frost brings it to two.

combat_skills.description: Burst in your movement direction to leave an attack's path. Save it for a committed shot or an encircling pack.

mastery.text: you recover from the dash sooner

combat_skills.description: A fast, narrow fire projectile that builds ignite. Lead a target and let the burn keep working.
combat_skills.design_purpose: The fire opener: a quick bolt whose hit is small but whose ignite burns for seconds. It does not fork by itself - a Forked Lattice roll (projectile tag) gives it the orb's split, which is the kind of cross-skill grammar D-016 is for. Three bolts ignite a plain mob.

combat_skills.description: A close physical attack that builds bleed. Cut a pursuer, then move while it suffers.
combat_skills.design_purpose: A heavy strike that trades hit damage for bleed: two rends open a wound, and a bleeding mob that keeps chasing takes the moving multiplier - the anti-kite answer to D-012's stupid-zombie trains. Being an attack it also shatters frozen mobs.

combat_skills.description: Chill a full ring around you. Catch enemies behind as well as in front and prepare a freeze.
combat_skills.design_purpose: A ring of cold around the caster (cone_degrees 360 in combat_realtime.json): low damage, chill on everything close. Three novas freeze a ring bare, two with Deep Frost; with an orb in the mix it is the panic button that sets up a shatter with any attack.

combat_skills.description: Cash in frozen enemies around you with a shattering ring. Bosses take the limited boss response.
combat_skills.design_purpose: The owner's missing verb (3 Sep 2026): a ring that cashes in what cold set up. Its own damage is a whisper; it carries the shatter tag, and grammar.json lets a shatter-tagged skill trigger the hook, so every frozen enemy in the ring shatters and the novas cascade. Wide Shatter and every shatter modifier excite it. Long cooldown: it is the sentence's full stop, not its verb.

combat_skills.description: Three arrows spread across a front. Each enemy can be hit once per fan; spread the pack instead of crowding one target.
combat_skills.design_purpose: 5 Sep skill expansion: Three arrows spread across a front. Each enemy can be hit once per fan; spread the pack instead of crowding one target. Payload and cooldown control per-target power and recovery; projectiles/pierce/arc are base grammar values. Mastery follows existing use milestones; drop_weight is relative among unknown pages, with starting kits unchanged.

design_purpose_mastery: Skill mastery (D-019): each combat skill has use-milestones, and each milestone unlocks one perk - a modifier from items.json at a flat value that applies to this skill alone (the grammar tags every skill with skill:<id> for that). Uses count in the sim (a cast that fired), ride in the save, and the HUD announces a perk when it arrives. Perks are the third door of every big mechanic: an item tier, a Foundry line, a mastery perk each give the small version; together the full one. Numbers stay inside the threefold budget.
